disclaimer: Attack verdicts are unrefereed model self-reports. An ill-posed label is a diagnostic of the catalog statement supplied to the model, not a literature-review status or a peer-reviewed result.

results.one_line: The catalog item is a research direction rather than a proposition, since “near-extremal,” “large piece,” and “based on a projective plane” have no specified quantitative meanings.
results.caveats: The auxiliary results below require linearity and balanced part sizes and do not settle an additive-stability formulation.

results.one_line: The catalog item is a research programme rather than a quantified conjecture; moreover, one natural universal Kendall-tau formulation is false in the canonical sampling model.
results.caveats: The negative result below concerns property-independent canonical induced-subpermutation testers, not fixed-property polynomial bounds or adaptive value-query models.

results.one_line: As written, the claim is elementary for every m at least 2 with n=1, while including m=1 makes it false.
results.caveats: The catalog statement almost certainly reverses an arrow or misplaces a quantifier.

results.one_line: Without a formal definition of “probabilistic methods” and “on their own,” the stated methodological forecast has no determinate mathematical truth value.
results.caveats: This does not settle the Δ+2 conjecture; only a narrow obstruction to the canonical direct LLL setup is proved below.

results.one_line: As extracted, the question has no determinate truth value because avoidability is defined only for induced path occurrences and no corresponding predicate is specified for non-path graphs.
results.caveats: A finite nonempty two-rooted reformulation could be genuine; below I prove only bounded-family obstructions under one explicit model.

results.one_line: The catalog item is an informal research expectation rather than a proposition, because neither “very few” nor “will end up” specifies a mathematical quantifier or asymptotic notion.
results.caveats: Universal, finite-exception, and density-one reformulations are distinct genuine conjectures and remain unresolved.

results.one_line: The quoted conjecture has no determinate truth value, and the most direct uniform finite-group formulation is false.
results.caveats: The counterexamples exploit precisely the unspecified infinite-complexity and torsion/trivial-solution exclusions, so a suitably repaired formulation may remain open.

results.one_line: The quoted belief has no fixed quantifiers or specified hopper variant, although the natural strong-hopper reading forces a rigid two-unit genus-jump configuration.
results.caveats: The conditional reductions below do not decide existence under the source paper's intended conventions.

results.one_line: The quoted sentence is a programmatic methodological suggestion, not a proposition with specified hypotheses, conclusions, or quantifiers.
results.caveats: A particular formalization could become a genuine graph-theoretic problem, but none is specified here.

results.one_line: The quoted remark does not specify a forbidden family or an if-and-only-if assertion, so it has no determinate truth value as a conjecture.
results.caveats: A precise completeness conjecture may be recoverable from the paper's defined examples, but it is not present in the supplied statement.

results.one_line: The prose claim has no truth value as stated, and its natural absolute-threshold interpretation is false even for connected simple bipartite cubic graphs.
results.caveats: Only absolute or sufficiently low order-dependent counting thresholds are ruled out; no probabilistic, normalized, or high-connectivity meaning of 'tend' was specified.

results.one_line: The modal claim has no definite truth value; under the natural fixed-width, supplied-sequence formulation, a constant-factor MIS approximation is equivalent to a PTAS and its existence remains open.
results.caveats: No MIS PTAS or fixed-width hardness is proved; the powering argument assumes a supplied contraction sequence.

results.one_line: With the displayed minimum over all n-vertex graphs, m(n,k)=0 identically, while replacing the minimum by a maximum gives a meaningful problem for which only partial results are established below.
results.caveats: This assumes open neighborhoods and induced edges on their union; the catalog may have transcribed max as min.

results.one_line: Under the literal unrestricted definition, m(n,k) has an elementary exact formula, contradicting the quoted n^2/(ek) bound and showing that an H-free hypothesis or some other restriction is missing.
results.caveats: This resolves the formulation supplied here, not the undefined parameter intended in the source paper.

results.one_line: The phrase “similar growth” specifies no asymptotic equivalence, and while the same-parameter Theta interpretation is false, plausible logarithmic or polynomial-equivalence versions remain open.
results.caveats: The argument uses the standard normalization in which N_DFL bounds the number of triangles; edge-count and endpoint conventions only change constants or parameter rescalings.

results.one_line: The phrase "not best possible" has no quantified meaning; the bound is literally improvable for p=2 and k=1, but the intended nondegenerate asymptotic claim is unspecified.
results.caveats: No improvement is obtained for p>=3 and k>=2, and the unverified 2025 article is not used.

results.one_line: Without an independent definition of twin-width for rational matrices the claimed equivalence is tautological or undefined; bounded grid rank does satisfy it over every infinite field, while the natural equality-contraction extension is false.
results.caveats: The full source question is truncated, and the grid-rank conclusion uses the precise definition stated below.

results.one_line: A weak finite-Grassmannian interpretation is trivially true, whereas a faithful stable interpretation requires an unspecified compatible family and already encounters a concrete obstruction for the graph K2.
results.caveats: The sign convention, ambient Grassmannian, stabilization, and meaning of subvariety are unspecified; the likely intended scheme-theoretic stable problem remains open.

results.one_line: Literally every graph H works by taking H'=H; under the natural requirement H' not isomorphic to H, I prove that every complete graph K_r has the larger witness 2K_r on the class of nonempty graphs.
results.caveats: The intended extra condition on H' is absent; the witness 2K_r is disconnected and fails if the null input graph is allowed.

results.one_line: With no graph class specified the question has no single answer, and its universal interpretation is false even for the hereditary class of split graphs.
results.caveats: The counterexamples settle only the universal reading; they do not characterize all classes with bounded ratio and may overlap known negative examples.

results.one_line: As written, the claim is vacuous via the K_1 solution, and uniform FPT testing in fact yields a polynomial-time approximation with ratio o(OPT) by a timeout construction.
results.caveats: The catalog omits the required restriction on f; no claim is made about a prescribed elementary, power-type, or certifying guarantee.

results.one_line: As quoted, the conjecture omits essential bounds and quantifiers and hence has no truth value, although natural level-zero and structured special cases admit rigorous coverings.
results.caveats: The exact Conjecture 15 is absent; the conditional results below do not close the global quadratic-in-doubling complexity gap.

results.one_line: The catalog item is a schematic research programme rather than a quantified conjecture, since neither the connectivity class, the containment relation, nor the permitted obstruction type is specified.
results.caveats: Under the standard crossing-free definition, an exact dual criterion and a complete strongly connected 3-connected special case are proved below.
